hints.title: Subarray Contiguity After Sorting
hints.text: Sorting the array ensures that any retained balanced subset forms a contiguous subsegment.

hints.title: Ratio Boundary Condition
hints.text: Fix each index as the minimum value and find the rightmost element that does not exceed k times this minimum.

hints.title: Max Window Retained
hints.text: Track the maximum window size of valid elements and subtract it from the total array length.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def minRemovals(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        nums.sort()
        n = len(nums)
        max_kept = 0
        
        # For each element as minimum, find upper bound of elements <= nums[i] * k
        for i in range(n):
            target = nums[i] * k
            # Find rightmost index with value <= target
            idx = bisect.bisect_right(nums, target)
            max_kept = max(max_kept, idx - i)
            
        return n - max_kept
```

complexity.notes: Sorting takes O(N log N), followed by binary search for each element.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all non-contiguous combinations requires exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place sorting eliminates auxiliary collection overhead.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Leverage sorting to transform subset selection into contiguous range queries.
